title: Kids story - Kiko and the Kite

parts.style: warm, gentle storytelling welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Hello again. <short pause> Are you ready for a story? <short pause> Tonight's story is about a girl named Kiko, a windy hill, and a kite that just would not fly.

Kiko lived in a little town with lots of hills. <short pause> And every spring, all the children climbed the tallest hill to fly their kites. <short pause> Red kites, yellow kites, kites shaped like fish and birds and dragons, all dancing in the sky.

This year, Kiko wanted to make her very own kite. <short pause> So she found two thin sticks, some paper, a ball of string, and a long ribbon for the tail. <short pause> She cut, and she folded, and she glued. <short pause> And when she was finished, she held it up and smiled. <short pause> It was perfect.

parts.style: gentle, slow, painting a calm scene
parts.text: Kiko ran all the way to the top of the hill. <short pause> She held the string tight, and she ran as fast as she could. <short pause> The kite lifted up... <short pause> up... <short pause> and then, flop. <short pause> It fell right down into the grass.

Kiko tried again. <short pause> Flop. <short pause> And again. <short pause> Flop. <short pause> Her cheeks were red, and her legs were tired. <short pause> Some of the other children giggled. <short pause> Kiko's eyes filled with tears. <short pause> Maybe, she thought, I should just give up.

She sat down in the grass, holding her crumpled kite. <short pause> Just then, an old man who was walking his dog stopped beside her. <short pause> That's a fine kite, he said. <short pause> It doesn't fly, said Kiko sadly.

The old man looked at it carefully. <short pause> Hmm, he said. <short pause> Every time it falls, it's telling you something. <short pause> Let's listen. <short pause> Maybe the tail is too short. <short pause> Maybe the string is in the wrong place. <short pause> Falling isn't failing. <short pause> It's just learning.

So Kiko went home and tried again. <short pause> She made the tail longer. <short pause> She moved the string a little higher. <short pause> The next day, she ran up the hill. <short pause> The kite went higher this time... <short pause> but then it wobbled, and fell. <short pause> Kiko didn't cry. <short pause> She thought, What is it telling me now?
She added a little more paper to one side, to make it even. <short pause> She tied the knots tighter. <short pause> Day after day, she tried, and fixed, and tried again.

And then, one bright, breezy morning, Kiko ran down the hill, let go of the kite... <short pause> and it rose. <short pause> Up past the trees. <short pause> Up past the rooftops. <short pause> Up, up, up, until it was a tiny speck dancing among the clouds, with its long tail waving hello.

Kiko laughed and laughed. <short pause> And the children who had giggled before came running over. <short pause> How did you do it? they asked. <short pause> Kiko smiled. <short pause> I just didn't stop trying, she said. <short pause> Come on, I'll show you.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Kiko learned something important on that hill. <short pause> When something is hard, it doesn't mean you can't do it. <short pause> It just means you haven't done it yet. <short pause> Every try, even the ones that fall, helps you get a little closer.
I wonder... <short pause> is there something you're still learning to do? <short pause> Remember Kiko, and keep trying.
That's the end of our story. <short pause> Goodnight.
